``format_table`` writes a header line, a delimiter line, and one line per
row, separated by ``\\n`` with no trailing newline. Every line is ``| ``,
then the column cells joined by `` | ``, then `` |``.

Cell text is ``str(value)``, or empty for ``None``, with each ``|``
escaped as ``\\|``. A row shorter than the header is padded with empty

(in that order, each optional), then optionally ``T`` followed by time parts

"""Read INI configuration files.

The text is read line by line:

- Blank lines, and lines whose first non-space character is ``#`` or ``;``,
  are ignored, and end any value being continued.
- ``[name]`` (surrounding whitespace allowed) starts a section. Section
  names are stripped and case-sensitive. A section that appears again
  continues the earlier one.
- ``key = value`` or ``key: value`` sets a key in the current section,
  splitting at the first ``=`` or ``:``, whichever comes first. Keys are
  stripped and lowercased, values stripped; a key appearing again in a
  section replaces the earlier value.
- A line starting with whitespace, directly after a key line or another
  continuation line, continues that key's value: its stripped text is
  appended after a ``\\n``. Any other line is read as above after
  stripping it.

A key before any section, a line that is none of the above, or an empty
key raises ``ParseError`` with the 1-based line number.

After the whole text is read, values are interpolated: ``${key}`` is
replaced with the value of ``key`` in the same section, ``${section:key}``
with the value from another section, and ``$$`` with a literal ``$``
(which is not interpolated further); any other ``$`` is left as it is.
Interpolation is recursive: referenced values are interpolated too. A
reference to a missing key or section, or a cycle, raises
``InterpolationError``. Keys inside references are lowercased like other
keys.

``parse`` returns a dict of section names to dicts of keys to values, with
sections and keys in the order they first appear.
"""

from __future__ import annotations


class ParseError(ValueError):
    def __init__(self, lineno: int, message: str):
        super().__init__(f"line {lineno}: {message}")
        self.lineno = lineno


class InterpolationError(ValueError):
    pass


def parse(text: str) -> dict[str, dict[str, str]]:
    """Parse INI text."""
    raise NotImplementedError

def raises(f, *a, **k):
    try:
        f(*a, **k)
    except ValueError:
        return True
    return False


# basic + defaults
assert format_table(["a", "b"], [[1, 2]]) == "| a   | b   |\n| --- | --- |\n| 1   | 2   |"
# alignment padding, center odd space on right
out = format_table(["x", "y", "z", "w"], [["ab", "ab", "ab", "ab"], ["abcdef"]],
                   ["left", "right", "center", None])
assert out.split("\n") == [
    "| x      |   y |  z  | w   |",
    "| :----- | --: | :-: | --- |",
    "| ab     |  ab | ab  | ab  |",
    "| abcdef |     |     |     |",
], out
assert format_table(["h"], [["ab"]], ["center"]).split("\n")[2] == "| ab  |"
assert format_table(["head"], [["a"]], ["center"]).split("\n")[2] == "|  a   |"
# delimiter widths
assert format_table(["abcde"] * 4, [], ["left", "right", "center", None]) == \
    "| abcde | abcde | abcde | abcde |\n| :---- | ----: | :---: | ----- |"
assert format_table(["a"] * 3, [], ["left", "right", "center"]).split("\n")[1] == "| :-- | --: | :-: |"
# None cells
assert format_table(["a", None], [[None, "x"]]) == "| a   |     |\n| --- | --- |\n|     | x   |"
# pipe escaping counted in width
assert format_table(["a"], [["x|y|"]]) == "| a      |\n| ------ |\n| x\\|y\\| |"
# long rows rejected; bad align
assert raises(format_table, ["a"], [[1, 2]])
assert raises(format_table, ["a", "b"], [], ["left"])
assert raises(format_table, ["a"], [], ["left", "left"])
assert raises(format_table, ["a"], [], ["middle"])
assert raises(format_table, ["a"], [], ["Left"])
# round trip
h, r, al = ["name", "a|b", "n"], [["x", "p|q", 3], ["long value", None]], ["left", "center", "right"]
assert parse_table(format_table(h, r, al)) == (
    ["name", "a|b", "n"], [["x", "p|q", "3"], ["long value", "", ""]], ["left", "center", "right"])
assert parse_table(format_table(["a"], [])) == (["a"], [], [None])
# missing pipes, irregular padding
assert parse_table("a|b\n:-|-:\n1|  2  ") == (["a", "b"], [["1", "2"]], ["left", "right"])
assert parse_table("  |a |   b\n|---|:---:|\n 1 |2|\n") == (["a", "b"], [["1", "2"]], [None, "center"])
assert parse_table("a | b |\n- | - |\n x\\|y | z") == (["a", "b"], [["x|y", "z"]], [None, None])
assert parse_table("a\n-") == (["a"], [], [None])
assert parse_table("| a\\| |\n| --- |\n| \\|\\| |") == (["a|"], [["||"]], [None])
# errors
for bad in ["", "| a |", "| a |\n| b |", "| a |\n| : |", "| a |\n| ::- |", "| a |\n| -:- |",
            "| a | b |\n| --- |", "| a |\n| --- | --- |", "| a | b |\n| - | - |\n| 1 |",
            "| a |\n| - |\n| 1 | 2 |", "| a |\n|  |", "a\n- -"]:
    assert raises(parse_table, bad), bad
print("ok")

I implemented `format_table` and `parse_table` in `/private/tmp/tmp8t2bvjra/pete/projects/devkit/devkit/table.py`, and my assertion script passes on Python 3.9.6. That was the only repo file I edited, and the signatures and docstrings are unchanged.

**What I implemented**
- **`format_table`** builds the cell text from `str(value)`, uses an empty string for `None`, and escapes `|` as `\|`. It pads short rows with empty cells and rejects long rows. Each column is as wide as its longest cell (escapes included) and at least 3. It pads cells by alignment, writes the delimiter row with colons, and joins the lines with `\n` with no trailing newline.
- **Bad `align`:** an unknown value or the wrong length raises `ValueError`. Case matters, so `"Left"` is rejected.
- **`parse_table`** splits cells on any `|` that doesn't have a `\` directly before it. It accepts tables with or without leading and trailing pipes, strips each cell, and turns `\|` back into `|`. Each delimiter cell has to match `:?-+:?`. It raises `ValueError` if there are fewer than two lines, if a delimiter cell is bad or the delimiter line has a different number of cells than the header, or if a data row has a different number of cells than the header.
- I added four small private helpers to keep it short.

**Spec ambiguities and how I resolved them**
- **Blank lines at the start or end:** I strip the whole text before splitting it into lines, so a trailing newline is fine. A blank line in the middle of the table becomes a one-cell row, which fails the cell-count check unless the table has one column.
- **Rows must match the header exactly when parsing:** a short row is an error, even though `format_table` pads short rows. That is what the spec says.
- **Backslash before a pipe:** `\|` always counts as an escaped pipe. If a cell ends in a literal backslash and there's no space before the next pipe (e.g. `a\|`), it's ambiguous, and it gets read as an escaped pipe. Output from `format_table` always has a space there, so round-tripping is unaffected.
- **Single column with no pipes:** a line with no pipes at all (e.g. `a` above `-`) is read as a one-column table.
- **Empty header:** not covered by the spec. `format_table([], [])` just produces lines like `|  |`, and I didn't add a check for it.
